clue.text: Money set aside to finance submarine warfare?

definitions.text: Money set aside to finance submarine warfare?

parts.words: Money set aside to finance submarine warfare?
parts.note: a fund that pays off a debt is read literally as cash for sending ships to the bottom

explanation.surface: A naval budget earmarked for torpedoing enemy vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The real term is a financial one: money put aside regularly to repay a debt. The question mark invites the literal reading of a fund for sending ships down.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund of this kind is accumulated savings set aside to repay a loan or replace assets.

clue.text: Misfortunes that make us sick

definitions.meaning: troubles or bad luck in general
ailments and diseases, which make a body unwell

explanation.surface: Bad luck that leaves us feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both troubles in life and bodily ailments that cause sickness.

clue.text: A sign that visitors are unwelcome

definitions.text: A sign that visitors are unwelcome

parts.words: A sign that visitors are unwelcome
parts.note: the words describe the notice on a gate warning strangers away

explanation.surface: A notice telling callers they are not wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-word instruction is the usual wording on a notice forbidding entry to strangers.

clue.text: A point that's hard to drive home

definitions.text: A point that's hard to drive home

parts.words: A point that's hard to drive home
parts.note: sounds like an argument that is difficult to make; literally a hard metal spike that a hammer drives in

explanation.surface: An argument someone struggles to get across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' and 'drive home' suggest debating; the thing meant is a hard pointed spike that is hammered in.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's spike has a sharp tip and is hammered fully into wood.

clue.text: FBI agents housed in suitable fabrication

indicators.note: the agents are lodged inside the word for suitable

parts.note: suitable means fit
G-men is American slang for federal agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: Federal agents lodged in a fitting invention.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something invented by the imagination, a fabrication rather than fact.

clue.text: A snare put out lor farm animals

indicators.note: put out means disordered, so the letters of a and the trap are rearranged

parts.note: a snare is a trap such as a net

explanation.surface: A trap is laid to catch livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges A and NET into a word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, the oxen and cows kept on a farm.

clue.text: Provision for a temporary settlement

parts.note: sounds like a legal or financial arrangement; really a place laid out for pitching tents for a short stay

explanation.surface: An interim financial arrangement in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests a payment that ends a dispute; here it is a group of tents set up for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground set aside for tents provides a place where campers settle for a few nights.

clue.text: Suitable retirement present for a scoutmaster

definitions.text: Suitable retirement present for a scoutmaster

parts.words: Suitable retirement present for a scoutmaster
parts.note: retirement read as going to bed, the gift being bedding a scout would take camping

explanation.surface: A fitting leaving gift for a scout leader who is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work, but it is retiring for the night; scouts sleep in these on camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded zip-up bed roll is what scouts sleep in under canvas, so it suits going to bed.

clue.text: A jumbo-size seal?

parts.note: jumbo is a nickname for a big animal of the trunked kind, and the largest seal is named after it

explanation.surface: Asking about an extra-large stamp or seal.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo, the famous London Zoo animal, made the name a byword for something huge; the largest seal has a trunk-like nose and the same animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest kind of seal has a dangling snout like a trunk and enormous bulk.

clue.text: Pack up work for the rest of the year?

definitions.text: Pack up work for the rest of the year?

parts.words: Pack up work for the rest of the year?
parts.note: pack up work sounds like quitting, but means packing a case for a break, rest of the year being the annual rest

explanation.surface: Giving up work for the remaining months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest of the year' reads as the remaining months; it is the year's rest, the annual break, for which one packs a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the annual break from work means leaving with luggage for a vacation.

clue.text: Go-ahead messengers who make way for others

definitions.text: Go-ahead messengers who make way for others

parts.words: Go-ahead messengers who make way for others
parts.note: messengers sent on in front who prepare the path for those following

explanation.surface: Enterprising couriers who step aside to let people pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go-ahead' sounds like enterprising and 'make way' like stepping aside; read literally, they go ahead and prepare the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Heralds sent in front announce or prepare for those who follow, as predecessors do.

clue.text: Ruthlessly cuts down a sex revolution?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of a sex are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sexual revolution ruthlessly cuts something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges the letters of A SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop jobs or projects without mercy is to give them the chop, as with a woodsman's tool.

clue.text: Go back into a West relic

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Go back into a West relic' is garbled OCR (likely 'a West African republic'); no scan or reprint gives the wording that supplies the TO round the reversed GO.
annotationWithheld.clue: Go back into a West relic

clue.text: The bonus to be paid before take mother out

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'The bonus to be paid before take mother out' has a word missing (probably 'I' before 'take'); without the printed wording the indicator for putting I in MUM cannot be parsed.
annotationWithheld.clue: The bonus to be paid before take mother out

clue.text: Commissioned wearer of the crown

parts.note: sounds like a monarch; really an army officer whose rank badge is a crown

explanation.surface: A monarch appointed to wear the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British Army this officer's rank insignia is a crown on the shoulder; 'commissioned' marks a commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissioned army officer ranking above captain wears a crown as the badge of rank.

clue.text: An Italian poet giving a a musical direction

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian poet issuing an instruction to musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'a' in the feed is a print slip; one serves as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo marking tells players to go at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: An arterial road of vital importance

definitions.text: An arterial road of vital importance

parts.words: An arterial road of vital importance
parts.note: sounds like a major highway; really the body's chief route for blood, vital being literally of life

explanation.surface: A trunk road essential to the transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial road' suggests a main highway; the body's largest artery is the route meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The great vessel carries blood from the heart to the whole body, so it is vital to life.

clue.text: Kind of picture card the sailor has to return

parts.note: tar is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: return means the little word to is turned back

explanation.surface: A seaman must give back a picture card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the little word round; tar for a sailor is old slang from the tarred pigtails and clothing seamen once wore.
explanation.definitionFit: These illustrated cards are used in fortune-telling and in old card games.

clue.text: A state that requires relief

parts.note: a condition of want or poverty that calls for help

explanation.surface: A country that requires aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation; it is a condition, that of want.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty or want is a condition that calls for help from others.

clue.text: Healing balm from Bristol University

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment produced by a West of England university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the run of letters across 'BrisTOL University'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolu is a fragrant balsam from a South American tree, used in cough mixtures and ointments.

clue.text: Expenses that are legally incurred

parts.note: outlays in general, and in particular the expenses of a lawsuit that a court awards

explanation.surface: Lawful outgoings.
explanation.definitionFit: A court orders the losing party to pay these, the legal expenses of a case.

clue.text: The skipper next in line for a 14 promotion?

definitions.meaning: the commander of a ship or team

definitions.text: next in line for a 14 promotion?
definitions.meaning: the army rank just below the one at 14, so in line to be promoted to it

explanation.surface: A ship's master due for a step up.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is MAJOR; the rank just below it in the army shares its name with a ship's master.
explanation.definitionFit: This rank commands a ship or team and is the army rank immediately below major.

clue.text: Rust put to use for surgical stitches

indicators.note: put here means set in a new order, so the letters of rust and use are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning rust to use as stitches in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' rearranges RUST and USE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons close wounds with these stitches.

clue.text: Erudite professor or one of his protégés, perhaps

definitions.text: Erudite professor or one of his protégés, perhaps

parts.words: Erudite professor or one of his protégés, perhaps
parts.note: the word covers both a learned academic and a pupil studying under him, perhaps one holding an award for study

explanation.surface: A learned don or one of his students.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a learned person and also a pupil or holder of a scholarship.

clue.text: Ai cut not normally on offer to the highest bidder

indicators.note: not normally says the letters are not in their usual order

explanation.surface: A cut of meat sold off to whoever pays most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not normally' rearranges AI CUT into AUCTI, and ON follows unchanged; an ai is a three-toed sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell goods publicly to whoever bids most is to put them under the hammer.

clue.text: Spanish wine for use on a 7, maybe

definitions.meaning: an old name for a deep red wine from Spain
7 is a camping site, where one pitches a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine to drink at another clue's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is CAMPING SITE. Tent was a dark red Spanish wine, used as communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old Spanish red wine and the canvas shelter pitched at a campsite.

clue.text: One more than one's double

parts.note: a double means two people; add one more and there are three

explanation.surface: Someone who outdoes their lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's double' sounds like a lookalike; read as a pair, adding one gives a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three is one more than a pair.

clue.text: In spring we never see her

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Saying a woman is never seen in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' takes the run across 'sprinG WE Never'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a word that stands for her.

clue.text: I knock back about a couple

indicators.note: about means the reversed knock goes round the letter I
back means the word for knock is turned round

parts.note: a knock is a rap

explanation.surface: A person drinks back a pair of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR; 'about' puts that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of a kind make a couple.

clue.text: Leap to make an excuse, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of leap could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Jumping at the chance to make an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a reason given in defence or excuse.

clue.text: Cautiously negotiate a pedestrian crossing?

parts.note: the phrase means proceed with care, read literally as walking carefully over a zebra crossing

explanation.surface: Crossing the road carefully at a zebra crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to act carefully; the question mark points to its literal sense of stepping carefully on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to proceed with caution, literally stepping with care.

clue.text: Sparkling performer on breakfast TV?

parts.note: a celebrity of early-morning television, really the bright planet seen before dawn

explanation.surface: A brilliant presenter on an early-morning show.
explanation.walkthrough: The bright planet Venus seen before sunrise has this name; 'performer' and 'breakfast TV' suggest a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus shining in the east before dawn is the bright light of early day.
